notes:
Summary: QueueCraft is a mid-market SaaS vendor powering customer support for several regional telcos. Heavy chat volume (100k+ incoming messages/day) — primary goal is aggressive chat deflection and automated ticket summarization to reduce L1 headcount. Cost sensitivity is very high: finance asked for clear unit economics (cost per deflected conversation, cost per summarized ticket).

Key technical asks / constraints:
- Workloads: mix of short chat deflection (quick replies, FAQ), longer agent-assist sessions (context windows ~2-4k tokens), and nightly batch summarization jobs for backlog.
- Targets: end-to-end avg latency for deflection < 400ms p95; agent assist latency < 200ms for KV lookups; throughput spikes up to 6x during promo windows.
- Cost controls: need batching/caching recommendations, quantization options for internal dedicated fleet, and real projections showing token-level spend vs expected deflection rate.
- Availability: absolute priority on graceful degradation under spikes — automatic fallback to smaller quantized models or cached responses.
- Tooling: must support tool-calling (ticket create/update ops), idempotency on side-effects, and easy traceability (audit logs per-customer request).
- Data: EU customer residency requirement for 30% of traffic; segmentation + routing needed.

What we demonstrated:
- Showed hosted API + dedicated routing model: primary hosted for most traffic, dedicated pool for EU/residency-sensitive customers.
- Presented Optimize recommendations: batching window heuristics, prefix/KV caching for frequent intents, and quantization benefits for dedicated GPUs.
- Walked through unit economics example: with 25% deflection, recommended batching + cache could reduce token spend by ~40% at peak.

Quotes and paraphrases: "We need hard numbers — if deflection costs more than a junior rep, no go." — Head of Ops.
"During promos we see a 6x spike; we can't have 5-min timeouts. Need guaranteed fallback behavior." — SRE lead.

Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot covering weekend peak (sat-sun), integrate prefix caching for top-200 intents, run quantized model on dedicated pool for deflection path, measure deflection rate and cost per converted ticket. SE to instrument token tracking and per-route cost telemetry.

Open items:
- Security: KMS integration and SOC2 artifacts to share with their procurement team (requested contract addendum).
- Data residency: need a clear routing policy for EU customers and guidance on private deployment if pilot shows performance sensitivity.
- Economics: finance wants per-conversation TCO table comparing hire-cost vs Redwood solution at multiple deflection rates.

Short actionables (AE notes):
- Deliver pilot cost sheet + weekend runbook by 2025-01-21.
- SE to provide quantization memory/latency tradeoffs and recommended GPU types by 2025-01-20.
- Get security package + KMS checklist into Drive link and ping procurement.

Stability & reliability concerns (CRM shorthand):
- Cache warm-up on first promo day — risk of cold cache causing latency spikes. Need pre-warm strategy.
- Tool-calling idempotency: their ticketing system can't tolerate duplicate creates. Must demo exactly-once semantics or compensating patterns.

Related artifacts: cost model spreadsheet (drive link), pilot runbook, Fireflies recordings of demo and security sync.
